topics.label: Lecture opening and introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening framing, contextualising the complement system within immunology and setting expectations for the lecture.

topics.label: Foundational principles and core components of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the foundational concepts and central biochemical mechanics that govern the complement cascade.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the upstream recognition mechanisms that trigger complement and drive surface deposition to reach the critical activation threshold.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the downstream mechanisms by which activated complement coordinates pathogen eradication and immune clearance.

topics.label: Regulation of complement on host cells
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory mechanisms that prevent complement activation from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical manifestations of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic surveys how specific deficiencies across the complement cascade produce distinct clinical pathologies and disease vulnerabilities.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion of the complement system
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the strategies used by pathogens such as Staphylococcus aureus to circumvent complement-mediated immunity.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the closing framing, concluding the lecture on complement and announcing the upcoming topic.
